newsitem.title: SPAIN: Most Spaniards back government's ETA policy -poll.
newsitem.headline: Most Spaniards back government's ETA policy -poll.

text.p: Most Spaniards reject talks with ETA guerrillas and the transfer of their prisoners to the Basque country, a key quarterly survey showed on Wednesday.
The survey, in El Pais newspaper, was carried out before ETA killed a young politician last weekend, sparking huge protests in Spanish cities.
Sixty-six percent of Spaniards support the conservative government's stance against negotiations with ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom).
The poll also showed sixty percent favour keeping ETA prisoners dispersed across the country, with just 26 percent backing their transfer to the Basque country -- a key rebel demand.

ETA abducted 29-year-old Miguel Angel Blanco on July 10 and said it would kill him if all ETA prisoners were not transferred to the Basque country within 48 hours. The threat was carried out shortly after the deadline passed.

The poll was conducted after the release earlier this month of Jose Antonio Ortega Lara, who was kidnapped and held for nearly two years by the group in another attempt to force a prisoner move and spur talks on an independent Basque state.

Some 87 percent of the 1,200 adults surveyed said an end to ETA remained distant, while 35 percent said the rebel group, responsible for some 800 killings in its nearly 30 year struggle for an independent Basque state, might never disappear.
